subject: Observability credits, retention slabs, and dashboard packaging — cost constraints
messages:
From: Rachel Gomez <rachel@stathub.io>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@stathub.io
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability credits/retention slabs and dashboard packaging — initial ask

Hi Logan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We liked the trace sampling dashboard and the KV-cache visualizations; they map well to our SRE signals. Procurement asked me to get a clear breakdown of observability add-ons (retention, tracing sampling, advanced dashboards) and how you price slab vs metered models. Two constraints on our side:

- We have a tight FY28 budget and are price-sensitive for add-ons — requires visibility into unit economics.
- Legal prefers a single SOW and wants commit tiers for storage credits (not per-token).

Could you share:
1) A simple comparison of slab tiers vs metered (cost per GB-month and effective per-100k-trace cost).
2) Any standard discounts for 12-month committments or pre-purchased credits.
3) How overages are handled and whether roll-up credits can be applied across teams.

We can share an internal usage projection if that helps (I can attach a CSV). Target timeline: procurement needs something by EOD next Thursday to hit our finance cycle.

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Gomez
Director, Platform Ops
Stathub

Attachment: stathub-usage-forecast-q3-q4.csv (we'll attach on follow-up)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Gomez <rachel@stathub.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability credits/retention slabs and dashboard packaging — initial ask

Hi Rachel —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a concise breakdown (PDF) and a sample SOW to speed procurement. High level answers below; see attachment for the full rate tables and example math.

1) Slab vs Metered (short):
- Slab: packaged retention tiers (e.g., 1TB/30d, 5TB/90d, 20TB/365d). Predictable monthly fee, best for steady ingestion. Effective cost/GB drops with larger slabs.
- Metered: true consumption billing (per-GB-month) with automatic rollover credits for pre-purchased bundles. Better for spiky workloads.

2) Discounts/Commitments:
- Standard: 10% off list for 12-month commits on slabs or pre-paid credits (>$50k ARR).
- Concession path: 15% for 12-month commit + 25% pre-pay on credits (negotiated at AE/AM level).

3) Overages & cross-team roll-ups:
- Overages billed monthly at the published metered rate; any pre-purchased credits are consumed first.
- We can pool credits across top-level accounts within a single SOW (requires account aliasing).

Proposal options (quick, see attached PDF for numbers):
A) Slab-Heavy: 5TB/90d slab + advanced dashboards (seatless) — 10% off list, +5k storage credits.
B) Metered-First: 50k GB-month credits pre-pay, 12mo commit, 12% effective discount and automated rollover.
C) Pilot: 3-month trial of advanced dashboards + free 200k trace sampling events; convert to slab at month 4.

Next steps: if procurement shares the usage CSV, Aditya and I will model expected unit economics and send a single-page SOW + DocuSign link. If you need a steeper concession, Kim (copied) handles pricing exceptions — happy to loop her in for an approval path.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mobile: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_Observability_Pricing_v2.pdf; SOW_Stathub_OBS_2028.docx

From: Rachel Gomez <rachel@stathub.io>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@stathub.io
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability credits/retention slabs and dashboard packaging — initial ask

Logan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the PDF. I ran the slab numbers with finance and two asks came up:

1) To get this approved in our FY28 plan we need at least a 15% discount on the combined package (slab + advanced dashboards) for a 12-month term.
2) For the first 6 months we need buffer credits for trace sampling — we expect a ramp and want to avoid surprise overages while we tune sampling thresholds.

Can you confirm whether the concession path you mentioned (15% + pre-pay) can be formalized without an enterprise legal review? Procurement wants to avoid lengthy redlines if possible. Also, what does the support SLA look like for dashboard incidents (response + resolution targets)?

If this can be done, I'll route to procurement and we can aim for signing within 10 business days.

-Rachel

Quoted from your PDF: "Concession path: 15% for 12-month commit + 25% pre-pay on credits" — is there flexibility on the pre-pay percent?

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Gomez <rachel@stathub.io>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability credits/retention slabs and dashboard packaging — initial ask

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for the clarity and the timeline. I'm Kimberly (Pricing & GTM), stepping in to formalize an offer that stays within your procurement constraints while protecting Redwood unit economics. Quick answer: we can do a single-SOW 12-month commitment with a structured concession. Details below (this message is intended to be copy/paste into procurement if helpful).

Offer (single SOW, Stathub):
- Package: 5TB retention slab (90d) + Advanced Dashboards (seatless, up to 25 dashboards) + Tracing sampling add-on.
- Term: 12 months with automatic renewal unless cancelled with 30d notice.
- Price: list price $78,000/yr. Concession: 15% off list = $66,300/yr.
- Credits: we will add a one-time 10,000 GB-month storage credit usable in first 6 months to cover ramp.
- Trace sampling: 300k free sampling events in first 90 days for tuning.
- Pre-pay flexibility: instead of 25% pre-pay, we can accept a 15% pre-pay on credits + standard net-30 invoicing for the remainder.
- Overages: billed at metered rate; pre-paid credits consumed first; any unexpected overage in first 3 months triggers a joint review and potential temporary rate cap.
- SLA: 1h P1 response, 4h P1 initial triage for dashboard incidents, P2 4h response. Full SLA language in attached SOW.

Conditions: this concession is contingent on a signed SOW within 10 business days and authorization to pool credits across your top-level accounts (we need aliasing). We can provide a DocuSign link for the SOW and an export-ready invoice for finance.

I'll attach a redline-friendly SOW and a one-page summary for procurement. Logan/Aditya will run the usage projection and confirm the effective per-GB math.

If this matches what procurement needs, I'll issue the DocuSign link and flag finance for the 15% pre-pay option you prefer.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Head, Pricing & GTM Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: SOW_Stathub_OBS_2028.docx; Redwood_Observability_Pricing_v2.pdf; sample-usage-projection.csv
